title: Partner substitution: behaviour changes when the partner is replaced
as_reported: Collusion emerges in 94% of trajectories across 10 models; controlled peer interventions show that collusion is shaped by peer behavior (abstract).
rationale: The interventional contrast measures inter-agent influence itself. Controlled design, 10 models, large number of trajectories. The demo has no coordination element, so the row gets a weight but does not enter a verdict.

title: Partner substitution as support for agreement
rationale: Agreement is a latent node: dependence on the partner is evidence for it only through an inference, and the study distinguishes explicit coordination from relaxation that responds to the partner without any agreement.

title: Explicit agreement recovered from a hidden channel
as_reported: Secret collusion via steganography is demonstrated (Motwani et al., title). In one third-party environment only 2 of 229 collusive episodes verbalise the coordination in the transcript (Rose et al., abstract).
rationale: If an explicit proposal and acceptance are decoded, the message is the agreement. Reliability is doubtful: decoding is shown in lab settings and the key must be established, and such handshakes are rare in emergent settings (2 of 229).

title: Hidden channel detected, no agreement text recovered
rationale: A channel shows secrecy or capacity, not what was agreed. A shared training history can produce the same code without any agreement (a focal point). Alternative state of T03: the two never occur in one case.

title: Price-level audit finds supracompetitive prices
as_reported: Any test whose input is a single agent's price or bid history has power exactly equal to its false-positive rate (abstract).
rationale: The source shows that such audits are blind to this conduct by construction, so a positive or negative result carries no information about agreement.

title: Excess residual correlation between agents' unexplained choices
as_reported: Residual correlation of +0.053 between two deployments of one model against +0.0001 across models, across twenty models from nineteen developers (abstract).
rationale: Detects coupling that price levels cannot, but the within-model excess is exactly what a shared model would produce, so it cannot separate agreement from common cause. Known confound, hence doubtful.

title: Shared-model coupling as an alternative explanation of similar behaviour
as_reported: Same measurement as T06, read in the other direction: similar behaviour arises between deployments of one model.
rationale: The measurement is solid (twenty models, developer-clustered interval). It only undermines support that rests on similarity (T05, T06), not interventional support (T02). The demo has no alternative-explanation criterion, so it is entered as an exculpatory item and used only in cases where support is similarity-based.

title: Internal-state probe shows the model recognises the true answer it does not report
as_reported: Across eight models from five families the probe recovers the recognised answer at 0.70 to 0.87 balanced accuracy and stays readable under several forms of concealment (abstract).
rationale: Reads knowledge of the true value directly, which is what the element 'knowledge, not error' asks for. Needs access to model internals and is a single preprint validated on open-weight models, hence doubtful. Source type M4 follows the pool; a mechanistic reading is closer to expert evidence.

title: Reasoning-token count differs between truthful and untruthful answers
as_reported: Three models answered 210 questions under prompts to answer truthfully, falsely or indifferently; truth-directed answers used fewer reasoning tokens. The authors state this does not yet establish a detector of spontaneous deception (abstract).
rationale: The behaviour was prompted, not spontaneous, and the authors name the gap themselves. Records of reasoning may also not reflect the real cause.

title: LLM judge reads the messages and reports collusion
origin: own run, not archived in this repository
report_element: E2 or E3 (verdict on the whole claim)
as_reported: Project notes of 2026-10-23: on NARCBench steganographic runs the judge flagged 1 of 20 and 2 of 20 collusive runs against 0 of 20 controls (Fisher p about 1.0 and 0.49). Not reproduced here.
rationale: A null result at n=20: the judge cannot be distinguished from zero. The judge's output is itself an inference from the messages. No element in the demo corresponds to a verdict on the whole claim.

title: Sequence-level monitor detects structured misbehaviour that per-step monitors miss
as_reported: On a synthetic marginal-preserving sabotage attack, a per-step monitor scores AUC 0.52 and sequence-level monitors 0.79 to 0.97 (abstract).
rationale: The attack is a simulated construction on monitor scores, not real agent traces, and the result concerns detecting temporally structured misbehaviour, not whether the outcome differs from a world without collusion. The mapping to E4 follows the pool and is weak. The demo has no E4 element.

pool_ref: plus factor: change of customer or trigger
title: Same task for different customers: output quality differs
report_element: adjacent: single-agent conditional conduct, not collusion
as_reported: Project notes: US versus Chinese contractor persona 70% against 59% (p=0.03), ten comparisons without correction, none surviving Bonferroni at 0.005. Numbers not re-checked against the blog in this repository.
rationale: A paired contrast shows that a trigger changes one model's conduct. It becomes evidence of agreement only when the manipulated variable is the partner agent (as in T01/T02), not the customer. Uncorrected multiple comparisons, hence doubtful.

title: Trace tampering
rationale: A gate, not evidence. Abstract: all tested harnesses except one allowed agents to delete their traces when asked. Used as a sensitivity test on logged evidence (M2): lowering reliability or authenticity.

title: Economic intervention to break collusion
rationale: A defence, not evidence. A refusal of a profitable deviation could be a 'contrary to self-interest' plus factor, but no such result was used.

title: Probe-the-object test and evidence confrontation
rationale: Our protocols. No results exist yet, so they carry no weight.

title: Elicitation of hidden state
rationale: Methods that induce the behaviour. They show susceptibility under induced conditions, not conduct in the case at hand.

title: Trajectory anomaly detectors
rationale: Listed in the pool but not read beyond the title in this audit.
